tip.en: A palengke is a permanent wet market with rows of stalls under one roof; a talipapa is a smaller, periodic one. It is busiest at dawn. Stall prices are set by each seller, so check two or three stalls.
A small family store, often in a home. Good for canned goods, cooking oil, salt and sugar, and you can buy single small units (tingi). It generally does not stock perishables that need a fridge.

Kadiwa is a Department of Agriculture program where farmers and co-ops sell directly to buyers at events and pop-up stores. One report lists highland vegetables and eggs. Ask a local where the next one is.

ingredients.en: 2 cups cooked rice, ideally chilled overnight

steps.en: Put garlic in the pan with the oil while it is still cool. Cook slowly until golden.
Mix the salt into the rice.
Add rice to the pan. Stir-fry 3 to 5 minutes.
Serve. Add an egg or a fish on the side if you have one.

ingredients.en: Toppings you have: green onion, fried garlic, calamansi

steps.en: Boil the water. Add the rice.
Simmer about 30 minutes, stirring now and then, until thick.
Stir in the salt, cook 2 more minutes.
Serve hot.

name.en: Chocolate rice porridge with fried dried fish

steps.en: Boil 2 cups water. Stir in sugar and tablea until dissolved.
Add salt and the rice. Return to a boil.
Simmer on low until soft and porridge-like, stirring every 2 to 3 minutes. Add water if too thick.
Fry the tuyo until crisp. Watch it, it cooks fast.
Serve the porridge with the fish.

ingredients.en: 1/3 cup rice and 1/3 cup sticky rice
Green onion and calamansi to finish

steps.en: Fry the garlic in oil until golden. Set it aside for topping.
In the same oil, soften onion, add ginger, then brown the chicken. Add fish sauce.
Stir in both rices, add water, cover and bring to a boil.
Simmer on lowest heat 35 minutes or more, stirring sometimes, until the rice breaks down and it is thick.
Top with egg, fried garlic, green onion. Squeeze calamansi on top.

name.en: Mung bean stew with dried anchovies

ingredients.en: Rice, cooked separately in its own pot

steps.en: Soak the beans overnight.
Fry garlic, onion, tomato in oil. Add the dilis, cook 1 minute.
Add the beans and stir 1 to 2 minutes. Add water, boil, then simmer until the beans are soft and mushy. Add water if it gets dry.
Add fish sauce and pepper. Add spinach, cook 3 minutes.
Serve over rice.

name.en: Mung bean stew with dilis and malunggay

steps.en: Boil the beans in plenty of water 35 to 40 minutes until soft. Set aside.
In a second pot or after emptying the first, fry garlic and onion, add tomato, cook 2 minutes.
Add the dilis, then the cooked beans. Stir 2 minutes.
Add 1 to 2 cups water. Simmer 5 to 8 minutes.
Stir in malunggay, fish sauce and pepper. Cook 1 to 2 minutes. Serve over rice.

name.en: Mung beans with squash and malunggay

steps.en: Soak the beans overnight and drain.
Fry garlic until brown, add onion and tomato until soft.
Add the dried shrimp, beans, fish sauce and about 2 cups water. Cover and simmer until the beans are very soft.
Add the squash and cook until tender.
Stir in the greens, cook 1 minute. Serve over rice.

name.en: Mung beans in coconut milk with tofu and malunggay

steps.en: Fry garlic, onion and tomato in oil.
Add the beans, stir 2 minutes. Add water and boil. Simmer until mushy, adding water as needed.
Stir in the coconut milk, then the tofu. Cook 2 minutes.
Add malunggay, season with salt and pepper. Serve with rice.

ingredients.en: 1 tbsp oyster sauce or fish sauce

steps.en: Fry the tofu in oil until golden. Cube it, set aside.
In the same pan, fry garlic, onion and tomato until soft.
Add tofu back, then sprouts and carrot. Stir about 1 minute.
Add bell pepper 1 minute. Season with oyster or fish sauce and pepper.
Serve over rice.

name.en: Chicken ginger soup with papaya or chayote

steps.en: Fry garlic, onion, ginger. Add the chicken, brown about 5 minutes.
Add water, boil, cover and simmer about 40 minutes. Skim the scum and oil off the top.
Add papaya or chayote, cook 5 minutes.
Add the leaves and fish sauce, cook 2 minutes. Serve hot with rice.

ingredients.en: 1 bunch mustard greens or other leafy greens
Sinigang mix or other sour base

steps.en: Boil water. Add tomato and onion, cover, boil 5 minutes.
Add the fish, cook 5 to 7 minutes on low-medium.
Add radish, okra and green pepper, cook 5 to 8 minutes.
Add the sour base and fish sauce, then the greens. Cover, cook 4 minutes. Serve hot.
Fry onion and garlic (and ginger if you have it) until soft.
Add water, boil. Add tomato and bagoong, cook 3 minutes.
Add squash (and sweet potato if used), cook 7 minutes.
Add beans, okra, ampalaya and eggplant. Cover and cook 5 minutes.
Season with pepper. Serve with rice.

name.en: Squash and string beans in coconut milk

ingredients.en: 1 oz pork or dried fish, optional

steps.en: Brown the pork in oil if using. Fry garlic, onion, ginger.
Pour in coconut milk. Cover, boil, then simmer 5 minutes.
Add squash, cook 5 minutes.
Add string beans, cook 5 to 8 minutes so they stay crisp.
Season with fish sauce and pepper. Serve with rice.

ingredients.en: Sliced tomato and calamansi on the side

steps.en: Rub salt on the fish, inside too.
Heat the oil in a wide pan. Lay the fish in.
Cover with a small gap for steam. Fry each side 6 to 10 minutes on medium until crisp.
Serve with tomato, calamansi and rice.
Boil the coconut milk in a wide pot.
Add garlic, ginger, onion, fish sauce, pepper. Cover 5 minutes.
Lay the fish and peppers in. Cover and simmer on medium about 30 minutes.
Uncover and cook down the sauce to a small amount. Serve with rice.

ingredients.en: 1 bunch kangkong, stalks and leaves apart

steps.en: Fry the garlic golden. Keep some for topping.
Add onion until soft.
Add soy sauce, vinegar, water. Boil.
Add stalks, cook 2 minutes. Add leaves, cook 1 minute, cover 1 more.
Season with pepper, top with the saved garlic.

ingredients.en: 1 can sardines in tomato sauce (about 5 oz)

steps.en: Brown the garlic in oil. Add onion and tomato, 1 minute.
Add chayote, cook 2 minutes.
Fold in the sardines with their sauce, about 30 seconds.
Add water, boil, then simmer until the sauce is halved. Serve with rice.

ingredients.en: 1.5 ampalaya, halved, seeds removed, sliced thin

steps.en: To cut bitterness, soak the slices in warm salted water 5 to 8 minutes, rinse, squeeze gently.
Fry garlic, onion, tomato until soft.
Add the ampalaya, cook about 1.5 minutes.
Pour in the eggs, let sit 20 seconds, stir about 1 minute until just set. Serve with rice.

ingredients.en: 1/2 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 1 tbsp water
Calamansi to squeeze on the side

steps.en: Drain the tofu a few minutes.
Fry in hot oil until golden. Drain.
Leave about 2 tbsp oil. Fry garlic and chili 1 minute.
Add soy sauce, vinegar, water, sugar, pepper. Boil, do not stir for 3 minutes.
Stir in the cornstarch mix until thick. Pour over tofu. Serve with rice and calamansi.
Char the eggplant right on the stove flame, turning, until the skin is black and the flesh nearly soft.
Cool, peel, flatten with a fork.
Beat the egg with salt and pepper. Dip the eggplant.
Fry in the oil until medium brown. Pour the leftover egg on top, flip, brown the other side. Serve with rice.

title.en: Cook until hot all the way through

body.en: Color and texture are not reliable signs that food is done (seafood aside). The only sure check is a food thermometer: chicken should reach 165 F (74 C) inside.
Keep raw meat, poultry, fish and eggs away from ready-to-eat food. Use one board or plate for raw meat and fish, and wash it with hot, soapy water before using it for other food.

title.en: Build each day from four parts

body.en: Aim for a staple (rice), a legume (mung beans, tofu), vegetables or fruit, and some fish, egg or oil. WHO advice for adults is at least 400 g of fruit and vegetables a day, with pulses and whole grains as main carbohydrate sources.

title.en: Put vitamin C on the table with beans

body.en: Vitamin C helps the body take iron from plant foods such as beans and rice. FAO says each meal should have at least 25 mg of vitamin C. Tomato, calamansi and green vegetables in the same meal as the mung beans do this.
Fish sauce, shrimp paste, dried fish and soy sauce are already salty. WHO advises adults to keep salt under 5 g a day, so taste the dish first and add salty sauce a little at a time.

Follow your mission's water guidance first. If you must treat water: let cloudy water settle or filter it first, then bring it to a rolling boil for 1 minute (3 minutes above 6,500 feet, about 2,000 m). Cool and keep it in a clean, covered container.
Rinse fresh fruits and vegetables under running water before eating or cooking. Use safe water for rinsing. Use the same rule for herbs and greens like kangkong and pechay.
Wash with soap and clean water for at least 20 seconds before preparing food, before eating, and after using the toilet. If there is no soap and water, use a hand sanitizer with at least 60% alcohol.
The four steps: clean hands and surfaces, keep raw apart from ready-to-eat food, cook food fully, and chill perishable food promptly.

Do not leave perishable food out more than 2 hours, or 1 hour when it is hotter than 90 F (32 C). Without a fridge, cook amounts you will finish. Reheat leftovers to 165 F (74 C), checked with a food thermometer.

title.en: Diarrhea: ORS and when to tell the nurse

body.en: Use oral rehydration salts (ORS), mixed exactly as the packet says with clean water. Tell your mission nurse if you have blood in the stool or signs of dehydration (sunken eyes, drinking poorly, very sleepy). For how many days is too long, see the red flags card.

Carry a water bottle and refill it through the day. Pale yellow or clear urine usually means you are drinking enough. Rest in shade and do hard work in the coolest part of the day. Cramps, heavy sweating, dizziness, headache, weakness or nausea can mean overheating.
WHO's five keys for traditional food markets: keep clean, avoid contamination, keep food products safe, reduce contact with animals, and stay safe and protect yourself.

title.en: Red flags: contact your mission nurse now

body.en: Contact your mission nurse now if you have any of these: blood in your diarrhea, a high fever (over 102 F, about 39 C), vomiting so often you cannot keep liquids down, or signs of dehydration such as peeing very little, a dry mouth and throat, or feeling dizzy when you stand up. Also contact them if diarrhea lasts more than 3 days.
